guitar.evidence: Brian May's homemade "Red Special" guitar is one of the most iconic and well-documented instruments in rock history.

tone.target: razor-thin late-60s fuzzed rock attack with staccato bite
tone.profile: razor-thin late-60s fuzzed rock attack with staccato bite
tone.summary: A classic fuzzed rhythm chain using a Fuzz distortion into a Plexi-style amp model, paired with a 4x12 cabinet to achieve the aggressive, biting late-60s rock sound.

rig.name: Queen - Stone Cold Crazy - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in aggressive fuzz tones.
Provide initial grit and punch before the main fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here to simulate a slight boost/grit, as dedicated vintage preamps are limited. It helps tighten the attack.

alternatives.reason: A simple clean boost could also work.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the core 'fuzzed' texture and aggressive bite required for the late-60s sound.

alternatives.reason: Could provide a similar vintage grit, but Fuzz is more direct for the required texture.

blocks.purpose: Wah is explicitly avoided unless clearly heard; keeping it bypassed for maximum dryness and punch.
blocks.gap: The requirement was to 'drop wah unless clearly heard,' so the module is included but deactivated.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Plexi/Marshall style amp tone (UK 45/50 family) with punchy mids and controlled breakup.
blocks.gap: The UK SLP is chosen as a representative British rock amplifier model that fits the vintage, aggressive profile better than the US Deluxe or AC30 TB for this specific sound.

alternatives.reason: A strong alternative if UK SLP is too modern.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British rock cabinet sound and necessary punchy low-mids.
Enhance the 'bright cutting mids' and maintain a tight low end without sounding muddy.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more precise mid-range sculpting to achieve the required bite.

alternatives.reason: A simpler alternative, but less control over specific frequency ranges.

blocks.purpose: Lush modulation is explicitly avoided; keeping the module bypassed to maintain a dry and aggressive tone.
blocks.gap: The requirement was to avoid lush modulation, so this module is included but deactivated.

blocks.purpose: No specific delay effect was requested; keeping it bypassed to maintain maximum dryness and punch.
blocks.gap: The tone must be dry and aggressive. All time-based effects are bypassed.

blocks.purpose: Add a minimal amount of natural room ambience to prevent the tone from sounding completely sterile, while remaining dry.
blocks.gap: The goal is 'dry punchy staccato chords,' so reverb must be kept very low (20% mix) and decay time short.

alternatives.reason: Could add more definition, but Room better simulates a natural performance space.

blocks.purpose: Master volume control for final output level adjustment.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR to better capture vintage British cab realism.

proposals.recommendedAsset: vintage 4x12 UK/British IR (e.g., Vox or early Marshall)
proposals.reason: The current IR is generic; a specific vintage British cab will enhance the required Plexi bite and punch.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased realism and definition in the low-mids.
